chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who was hit in his ear, so he claimed that one of his ears had lost some of its hearing. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The struck ear is covered with a tight seal, and the healthy one is kept open. A bell is sounded towards his face, and it is said to him, 'Listen'. When the sound becomes hidden to him, its location is noted. Then it is sounded from behind him, and it is said to him, 'Listen'. When the sound becomes hidden to him, its location is noted. Then the distance between the two is measured. If they are equal, it is known that he has spoken the truth.'

Then he is taken to his right, and it is sounded until the sound becomes hidden to him, then its location is noted. Then he is taken to his left, and it is sounded until the sound becomes hidden to him, then its location is noted. Then the distance between the two is measured. If it is equal, it is known that he has spoken the truth.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then his damaged ear is opened, and the other is sealed well. Then the bell is sounded from in front of him, and it is noted where the sound becomes hidden to him. He is treated as he was treated the first time with his healthy ear. Then the excess of the healthy ear over the damaged one is measured by that calculation.'
ai.seo_question: How is hearing loss tested and quantified in Shia Islamic jurisprudence for compensation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details a precise, empirical methodology for assessing auditory impairment, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on objective evidence (bayyinah) in legal rulings such as calculating blood money (diyah). The procedure involves isolating each ear and measuring the distance at which sound becomes inaudible from various directions to quantify the deficit, demonstrating an early application of systematic medical-legal testing in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man was hit in his ear, so he claimed that one of his ears is deficient from hearing anything. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The struck ear would be covered up with an intense covering, and the correct ear would be kept open. So the bell would be sounded towards his face and it would be said to him, ‘Listen’. So when the sound is hidden to him, its place would be noted. Then it (the bell) would be sounded from behind him, and it would be said to him, ‘Listen’. So when the sound is hidden from him its place would be noted. Then it would be measured what is between the two. So if it was the same, it would be known that he is speaking the truth.

Then he would be seized by it from his right. Then it (the bell) would be sounded until the sound is hidden from him. Then its place would be noted. Then he would be seized by it from his left. So it (the bell) would be sounded until the sound is hidden from him. Then its place would be noted. There it would be measured what is between the two. So if it was the same, it would be known that he is speaking the truth.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Then his damaged ear would be opened up, and the other one would be closed with a new covering. Then the bell would be struck from in front of him. Then the sounds would be hidden from him, and he would be dealt with just as he had been dealt with the first time around, with his healthy ear. Then to find the difference of the hearing (abilities) of both ears to calculate a fair compensation on the basis of the differences that may have happened between the two ears.
